issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may reverse an acquittal when the trial court’s findings are perverse or contrary to the evidence, but should not disturb an acquittal where two reasonable views are possible.

A custodial statement is admissible under Section 27 of the Evidence Act to the extent that information supplied by the accused distinctly leads to the discovery of a fact previously unknown to the police.

An accused’s act of leading police to and identifying the place where evidence is recovered may be relevant as conduct under Section 8 of the Evidence Act, even if the accompanying statement is inadmissible.

In a circumstantial-evidence case, proof that the accused was last seen with the deceased may require the accused to explain the circumstances, and an unexplained failure may provide an additional link in the chain of circumstances.
The circumstantial evidence on record was sufficient to sustain the conviction for murder and the related offences, and the appellate reversal of the acquittal disclosed no ground for interference.
